sources_considered.why: Report of a June 2026 Jefferies research note: 12GW of US capacity scheduled for 2026 was under construction.
Primary CBRE release: 7,481 MW under construction in only eight primary North American markets in H1 2026.
BNEF: 23.1GW under construction globally and 15.9GW in the US at end-September 2025. Used as context because it falls before the target period.
Quotes the Sightline/Currence outlook, the likely origin of the 5GW figure. That figure covers only capacity slated for 2026.
CBRE H2 2025 figure (5,994 MW in primary markets at end-2025) falls before the target period. Consistent with the other evidence.
Restates the Currence 5GW-of-16GW finding. The publication date was not visible, so the Quintarelli post was used instead.
The page returned no article text, so the Cushman & Wakefield 31.7GW figure could not be cited.
The speaker's own post, read only to confirm the wording. It gives no source for the 5GW figure.

evidence_items.publisher: The Register (reporting a Jefferies research note)

receipt.public_excerpt: only 12 GW out of 24 GW of datacenter capacity scheduled for 2026 is currently under construction.

evidence_items.explanation: Jefferies counted about 12GW under construction in mid-2026 for 2026-scheduled US capacity alone. That is more than twice the '5GW at most' ceiling, even before adding projects due in 2027–28 that had started.

receipt.public_excerpt: The 7,481 megawatts (MW) under construction in H1 2026 surpassed the previous high reached in 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: Eight primary North American markets alone had about 7.5GW under construction in H1 2026. These markets exclude many large AI campuses elsewhere, so the total is higher still, and well above 5GW.

receipt.public_excerpt: As much as 23.1GW of capacity is under construction globally, split across 831 sites.

evidence_items.explanation: BNEF measured over 23GW of data center IT capacity under construction globally in late 2025. That is before the target period, but it shows the total under construction was far above 5GW shortly before the post.

evidence_items.publisher: Stefano Quintarelli blog (quoting Sightline/Currence Data Center Outlook)
evidence_items.locator: quoted excerpt from Sightline/Currence 'Data Center Outlook'

receipt.public_excerpt: At least 16GW of capacity is slated to come online in 2026 across roughly 140 projects. Yet only about 5GW is currently under construction.

evidence_items.explanation: This is the likely origin of the 5GW figure. It refers to the subset of large (>50MW) projects slated to come online in 2026, not all capacity under construction. It supports a narrow reading of the claim but not the plain one.

unresolved_gaps: No single authoritative global count of total AI data center capacity under construction in H1 2026 was found. The contradiction rests on subsets (US 2026-scheduled capacity; eight primary North American markets) that already exceed 5GW.
The $1 trillion revenue 'necessity' and the 30GW requirement are the speaker's model assumptions and were not tested.
Trackers define 'under construction' differently (IT capacity versus facility power; project size thresholds).
